newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha contango narrower due to short cover.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha contango narrower due to short cover.

text.p: Contango in near-term naphtha spreads narrowed in afternoon Tokyo trade on Monday amid revived buying interest for prompt cargoes, traders said.
Bids for the one-month spread from first-half August was heard at minus $1.00, against offers at minus 50 cents to even.
It was quoted at about minus $2.00 a few weeks ago.
The contraction in contango was partly attributed to short-covering by a regional trader for first-half August cargoes.
Open-spec naphtha barely moved on Monday amid lacklustre trading despite an overseas crude gain on Friday.
First-half September was assessed at $197.50/199.00 per tonne, little changed from late Friday's $197.00/198.50.
In middle distillate trading, high domestic stockpiles continued to keep traders from engaging in spot activity, market players said.
"No middle distillates are coming to Japan except for term cargoes," one trader with a trading house said.
He also said some refiners are likely to sell Middle Eastern term cargoes on an FOB (free on board) basis rather than bring them to Japan.
